name: mid-mobile-android-nometrics
note: Three years Android, entirely qualitative bullets with not one number in them, against a posting that wants Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose. Partial: the Android depth is real, the Compose and KMP are not there. This is the common real case and the strongest test of whether the rewrite invents metrics.
resume_text:
Nikhil Bhosale
Android Developer
Pune, Maharashtra | nikhil.bhosale@example.com | +91 20554 81093

ABOUT
Android developer with a little over three years on consumer apps. I have shipped to the
Play Store continuously across two companies and I am most useful on the part of the job
that is not writing features: crashes, ANRs, and the slow accumulation of things that make
an app feel bad on an older phone.

WORK EXPERIENCE

Thrivo Mobile, Pune
Android Developer | Sep 2023 - Present
- Work on the consumer app for a grocery delivery service, in the squad that owns the cart
  and checkout journey.
- Built the saved addresses and delivery slot selection screens, including the offline
  behaviour when the user has no signal at the door.
- Moved the cart screen off the old activity-and-fragment structure onto a single activity
  with the Navigation component, which removed a family of state restoration bugs.
- Introduced Hilt for dependency injection across the checkout module. Before that,
  objects were constructed by hand in onCreate and the module was almost impossible to test.
- Wrote unit tests for the cart pricing logic with JUnit and MockK, which the team has
  since extended to the promotions code.
- Handle Play Store release duties on rotation: staged rollouts, watching Crashlytics, and
  halting a rollout when the crash-free rate moves the wrong way.
- Worked with the backend team to move the checkout endpoints off a chatty design where the
  app made several calls in sequence before it could show a price.

Orbit Apps, Pune
Junior Android Developer | Jun 2022 - Aug 2023
- Built features for a fitness tracking app in Kotlin: workout history, a weekly summary
  screen, and reminder notifications through WorkManager.
- Integrated the Room database for offline workout storage and wrote the migrations when
  the schema changed.
- Consumed REST APIs with Retrofit and OkHttp, and moved the older AsyncTask code to
  coroutines.
- Fixed a long standing memory issue on the history screen that was holding bitmaps after
  the fragment was destroyed.
- Took part in design reviews with the product designer and pushed back where a layout
  would not hold up on small screens.

EDUCATION
B.E. Computer Engineering
Pune Institute of Computer Technology, Savitribai Phule Pune University
2018 - 2022

SKILLS
Languages: Kotlin, Java
Android: Android SDK, Coroutines, Flow, Room, Retrofit, OkHttp, Hilt, WorkManager,
Navigation component, ViewModel, LiveData, Material Design
Architecture: MVVM, clean architecture, repository pattern
Testing: JUnit, MockK, Espresso
Tools: Android Studio, Git, Gradle, Firebase Crashlytics, Firebase Analytics, Play Console

INTERESTS
I read the Android release notes properly every year, which is a strange hobby but it has
saved my team from two deprecation surprises.
jd_text:
Senior Android Engineer
Bengaluru or Remote (India) | Mobile Engineering

We make a personal finance app with about 2 million monthly active users in India. The
mobile team is fourteen people, split across Android and iOS, and we are in the middle of
a move to Kotlin Multiplatform so that the two platforms stop implementing the same
business rules twice and disagreeing about the edge cases.

The role
- Build features in our Android app, which is Kotlin, Jetpack Compose and a modularised
  Gradle setup with about thirty modules
- Contribute to the shared Kotlin Multiplatform layer: networking, persistence, and the
  domain logic that both platforms consume
- Take ownership of app health. Crash-free rate, ANR rate, cold start time and APK size are
  tracked per release and somebody has to care about them
- Work directly with design on motion and interaction rather than receiving a static spec
- Review code across the Android codebase, including modules you did not write

What we are looking for
- 4 or more years of Android development, shipping to the Play Store
- Kotlin as your primary language, including coroutines and Flow used properly rather than
  as a wrapper around callbacks
- Jetpack Compose in a production app. We are almost entirely Compose now and the remaining
  View code is on its way out
- Modern Android architecture: ViewModel, unidirectional state, dependency injection, a
  clear separation between UI and domain
- Dependency injection with Hilt or Koin
- Local persistence: Room or SQLDelight
- A real testing habit: unit tests, and some UI testing you did not abandon after a month
- Performance work: you have profiled something, found the cause, and fixed it

Would help a lot
- Kotlin Multiplatform, particularly if you have shipped it
- SQLDelight and Ktor client
- Gradle at the level of writing convention plugins, not just editing a build file
- Compose Multiplatform
- Some Swift or iOS familiarity, enough to talk to the other half of the team
- Experience with a modularised codebase and the build time problems that come with one
- Fintech, payments or anything where correctness of money arithmetic mattered

We interview with a take-home Compose screen, a code review exercise on our own code, an
Android internals conversation and a team fit call.
